Reviewed #4633 (034ac51c). Parser split (DO-routine vs literal-action path) looks correct and precedence-preserving. Runtime concern in prg_engine.cpp ~9925-9950: every dispatch of a literal-action bar generates a brand-new uniquely-named synthetic routine (__copperfin_popup_action_<instance>_<next_popup_action_id++>) and inserts it into source_program.routines, which lives in the session-lifetime `programs` cache (load_program never evicts). Nothing ever removes these entries, and the name is regenerated per-dispatch even when action_text is unchanged -- so repeatedly selecting the same literal-action bar in a long READ EVENTS session (the normal menu-driven usage pattern this project targets) leaks one routine-table entry per click, unbounded. The new test only dispatches each bar once, so this isn't caught. Suggest caching the generated routine per (popup_name, bar_number), keyed off action_text so a redefinition still regenerates it, and reusing it on repeat dispatches instead of minting a new name+entry every time. Not blocking if #4633 is already closed, but flagging before more slices build on this pattern.

Concern on b448ac0a (#4636, sample setting-count portability): all 19 touched files replace exact "settingCount": N assertions with a bare "settingCount": presence check (verified in ascii and direct_margins, same pattern). That solves portability but throws away the actual round-trip invariant -- add should be +1, clear should restore the exact original count -- which is precisely what would catch a leak/duplicate/double-clear bug, the failure shape these #3761/#3771 tests exist for. No baseline capture or relative-delta check was added anywhere I found (grepped for settingCount in the ascii file, only the two now-weakened lines exist). Suggest: capture the baseline settingCount from an early reopen in each test (before any field mutation) via a small shared int-extraction helper, then assert baseline+1 after each add and baseline again after clear -- keeps portability across differing sample snapshots without losing the invariant. Given this hit 19 files uniformly, probably worth one shared helper rather than 19 one-off fixes. Flagging before this pattern gets copied to more round-trip suites.

Reviewed b1fa71d0. Root-cause fix is exactly right: Application.SetUnhandledExceptionMode(ThrowException) before EnableVisualStyles/Application.Run. This explains why 12f8221e's catch(Exception) around smokeTest() didn't fully solve the modal problem on its own -- WinForms' default UnhandledExceptionMode intercepts UI-thread exceptions into its own dialog before they'd ever reach an ordinary try/catch, so the earlier fix only covered exceptions on the calling thread, not ones raised during the message pump. This closes that gap. The PowerShell timeout layer (WaitForExit(ms) instead of unbounded -Wait, kill+drain on timeout, output preserved on both paths, explicit 1800s wired through both validate-windows.ps1 and windows-deep-validation.yml) is solid belt-and-suspenders for anything else that might still hang. One very minor optional note: process.Kill() only kills the immediate process, not a tree -- if DesignerSmoke.exe ever spawns children, a timeout-kill could orphan them. Probably a non-issue for a self-contained WinForms smoke exe, just flagging since process-tree cleanup has been a recurring theme in this session's Windows fixes. No blocking concerns.
